To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
slice-selective RF shimming with a higher number of Tx channels improves imaging fidelity at UHF.
the use of a higher number of independent Tx channels in conjunction with slice-selective RF shimming can significantly increase the B1+ homogeniety and decrease the RF-power deposition at 7T.

RF shimming in human brain with 2-, 3- and 4-channel transmit yields an increase in RF-power by 2.6%, 4.5% and 5.7%, respectively, when compared with 1 channel transmit at 7T, and that slice-selective RF shimming yields a 43% increase in B1 homogeneity and/or reduces RF power by 68% at 7T.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of a higher number of independent transmit channels together with slice-selective radio-frequency (RF)-shimming to improve the B1+ homogeniety and to reduce the RF power deposition in the human brain in vivo at 7T.
the improvement of imaging fidelity by employing a higher number (i.e., 8) of independent transmit channels together with slice-selective RF shimming at UHF.
the effect on homogeneities and RF-power when using higher number of transmit channel configurations together with slice-selective RF shimming.

a higher number of independent transmit channels together with slice-selective RF-shimming can significantly reduce the RF power and/or improve B1 homogeneity at high field strengths.
the use of a larger number of Tx channels with slice-selective RF shimming yields a significant improvement in B1 homogeneity, which is accompanied by an overall reduction in RF-power deposition.
the higher the number of independent Tx channels, the higher is the homogeneity and/or lower the RF-power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of slice-selective radiofrequency shimming with a higher number of independent Tx channels can provide a substantial increase in B1 field homogeneity in vivo at UHF.
a higher number of independent transmit channels can be employed to increase B1+ homogeneities and/or reduce RF-power deposition.
a higher number of Tx channels and slice-selective RF shimming can improve B1+ homogeneities, which in turn can lead to improved imaging fidelity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RF shimming with 8-channel Tx and slice-selective approach can improve B1+ homogenization and RF-power deposition in human subjects at 7T compared to CP global RF shiming.
the use of higher number of Tx channels together with slice-selective shiming can be employed to improve B1+ homogeneities and/or reduce RF-power deposition at 7T.
slice-selective RF shimming is a powerful method for increasing B1+ homogeniety and reducing RF-power deposition at high fields.
